newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed sellers absent as prices ease.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed sellers absent as prices ease.

text.p: Northern European rapeseed sellers are absent from the market where spot prices have eased in line with the weaker Chicago soycomplex, brokers said on Friday.
"We saw a lot of business earlier this week but sellers have pulled out because of the lower price and buyers find the market overvalued and prefer soybeans and sunseed," one said.
Nominal free Hamburg sellers prices of old crop rapeseed were down three marks from last week at 472 marks a tonne, with buyers five marks down from last week at 465.
But new crop free Hamburg withstood the the weaker spot trend and was offered at 445 marks for July/August, up five, with buyers at 440 marks, also up five.

"Processors cannot be entirely sure of consistent soybean supplies from the Americas and they also want to hedge against possible weather and area losses in the 1997 European rapeseed crop," one broker said.
A private German rapeseed area survey issued earlier today put the winter acreage for food rapeseed at 681,000 hectares, up 2.6 percent from last year but 49,000 ha below a December survey.
Rape oil demand was beginning to benefit from its shrinking premium over soy oil but prices were still too unattractive for many domestic consumers, brokers said.ust
Rape oil ran at par with soy oil for May/July and August/September at midday in Rotterdam but kept a 0.25 guilder premium over soy for February/April per 100 kg fob mill.
The premium has come down from 1.75 guilders in early January.
February rapeseed buyers prices at points other than Hamburg were at 460-472.50 marks, with new crop buyers at 430-450 marks, depending on location.
The Matif futures market last showed February at 452 marks, May at 461 and August at 438.
February/April rape oil sellers remained unchanged from a week ago at 87.50 marks while May/July was off 0.25 marks at 88.25.
February meal ex Hamburg mills was at 32.50 marks per 100 kg, and March/April at 31.00 marks.
